title: Rabbi Yudan ben Tarfon (Disputed Reading)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 1:6 and Orlah 1:3 read: “Rabbi Yudan said: kad tarifan le-ovya.” Pnei Moshe reads Rabbi Yudan ben Tarfon; Ahavat Tzion VeYerushalayim on Sheviit proposes Rabbi Yudan bar Tarfon. But the Jerusalem Talmud’s wording seems more correct: “when they have grown in thickness,” as explained in the Arukh, under taraf. It cites Eichah Rabbah on “Those reared in scarlet,” with the phrase tarifin be-kakla. Hyman describes this as Greek, meaning nurtured and raised in scarlet garments.

notes.text: Hyman prefers a phrase meaning growth in thickness over treating the words as the name ben Tarfon. The Arukh’s Greek-language explanation is his cited explanation, not a newly verified etymology.

The consulted Guggenheimer Orlah 1:3 reads Rabbi Yudan be-rabbi Trifon le-ovyah; consulted Piotrków Penei Moshe likewise names Rabbi Yudan bar Rabbi Trifon while explaining thickness. These actual readings must be distinguished from Hyman’s preferred kad tarifan wording and ben/bar Tarfon reports. His Greek/Arukh explanation and Ahavat Tzion claim remain attributed, not an identity ruling.
